chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (mercy of God be upon him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Ibn Fudal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Hamzah ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In His Word, the Mighty and High: "And it is not for Allah to lead people astray after guiding them. He even makes clear to them what they should guard against." He (AS) said: "He makes them recognize what pleases Him and what angers Him."
And He said: "And inspired it with knowledge of evil and piety." He (AS) said: "He explained to it what it should do and what it should avoid."
And He said: "Surely We have shown him the way: he may be thankful or unthankful." He (AS) said: "He made us recognize what to accept or to avoid."

And concerning the Word of the Mighty and High: "And as to Thamud, We guided them, but they chose error above guidance." He (AS) said: "We made them recognize, but they consciously chose misguidance over guidance, while they knew."
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq interpret the concept of divine guidance and human choice in the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that divine 'guidance' (huda) in these verses denotes the clear exposition of God's will and the innate inspiration of the soul to distinguish between obedience and disobedience. This interpretation underscores the Shia doctrine of 'clear proof' (hujjah), where God ensures humanity possesses the cognitive capacity to recognize His commands before holding them accountable. The Imam further clarifies that the choice between gratitude and ingratitude arises from this prior recognition, emphasizing human agency within the framework of divine clarity.
